chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Sayf from Mansur who said: A trustworthy companion of ours narrated to me who said:

I was walking in some of the streets of Mecca when a man met me and said, 'Slaughter these two birds for me.' So I slaughtered them while I was in a state of Ihram (Halal), forgetting. Then I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said, 'The price is upon you.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الثَّمَنُ: The price or value, referring to the compensation paid for the killed animal.
key_terms.حَلَال: The state of Ihram, where a pilgrim is restricted from certain activities including hunting.

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for killing game while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-thaman* (monetary valuation) applied to a specific case of accidental game killing while in a state of Ihram. It highlights the scholarly distinction between intentional and unintentional violations, where the Imam (peace be upon him) prescribes financial compensation rather than ritual penalty, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding minor infractions during pilgrimage.
